source.title: PrivacyScalpel: Enhancing LLM Privacy via Interpretable Feature Intervention with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Ahmed Frikha; Muhammad Reza Ar Razi; K. K. Nakka; Ricardo Mendes; Xue Jiang; Xue-Bing Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and references. Some tables are flattened in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses neuron-level and SAE-feature interventions, but its results concern privacy leakage and utility—not neuron-pole interpretability, explanation faithfulness, or the attribution-graph claim in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layer-probe results and privacy/utility results for feature and neuron-level interventions. The layer-probe results select a layer for the method, and the intervention results measure PII privacy outcomes; neither measures a listed claim version. The rows below retain the explicitly described Gemma2-2b ablation comparison as a related finding, not a test of a listed version.
record.test_reason: A privacy-defence paper. It assumes model neurons are polysemantic and SAE features monosemantic, citing Bricken et al. 2023, but never measures any neuron's interpretability. It reports no explanation scores, no audit shares and no attribution graphs. Its results are PII leakage and QA utility under ablation and steering, so no listed version is tested. Those results could also come from intervention granularity rather than interpretability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE feature-level ablation and steering give a better privacy-utility trade-off than neuron-level interventions. They frame this as 'monosemantic features' beating 'polysemantic neurons', a premise taken from prior work and not measured here. Their 'neuron-level' baseline operates on residual-stream dimensions, not MLP neurons.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains k-sparse autoencoders and intervenes on latent features to reduce PII leakage; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing procedure described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention outcomes vary with model, intervention method, SAE use, and intervention settings such as feature count and steering intensity; the paper also reports different outcomes with reduced development data.

fits_no_version.finding: At layer 9 of Enron-fine-tuned Gemma2-2b, ablating 2,000 SAE latents and ablating 2,000 raw residual dimensions both cut email leakage to 0.01%. Utility is 58.05% with SAE versus 55.40% without, against no-defence utilities of 58.52% and 58.77%. Llama2-7b shows a smaller gap: 64.60% versus 63.48% at 0.0% and 0.05% leakage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating SAE latents removes PII leakage with less utility loss than ablating the same number of raw residual-stream dimensions.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The evidence concerns PII leakage and downstream utility rather than whether neuron poles have coherent, human-nameable jobs. Uncertainty estimates are not stated. Some table formatting is flattened in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: Other intervention configurations in Tables 1, 4, and 5 are not included because they report privacy/utility outcomes for methods and settings but do not measure any listed claim version; the layer-probe and SAE layer-replacement results likewise do not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron poles or of job shares in Qwen3-32B or any model.
No interpretability shares across models or scale. Gemma2-2b and Llama2-7b are used only for privacy defence.
No analysis of InceptionV1 or of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No measure of how architecture or tools affect interpretable-neuron share.
No attribution graphs and no neuron-based circuit explanation.
No test of explanations against held-out activations.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'assumes'. The paper takes neuron polysemanticity as given, the premise the essay contests, without testing it. No verdicts are given because nothing in the study measures how interpretable neurons are.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of neuron poles or shares of poles with one or multiple jobs.
No comparison of pole interpretability shares across models, architectures, or scales.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
No analysis of architecture, regularization, tool quality, or interpretability shares in vision models.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model-native neurons explain behavior without a replacement model or reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against activations or examples not used to produce them.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2b
rows.baseline: No defense: email leakage 5.15%; average utility 58.52%
rows.note: The text explicitly describes this as the same 2,000-feature ablation configuration without SAE. The outcomes measure privacy and utility, not neuron interpretability or the listed versions.
rows.check: Baseline is wrong. Table 1's no-defense utility without SAE is 58.77%, not 58.52%; 58.52 is the with-SAE column. Also, the 'without SAE' intervention zeroes residual-stream dimensions at layer 9: 2,000 of Gemma2-2b's roughly 2,304 dims. These are not MLP neurons or neuron poles, so the row measures nothing about neuron interpretability.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2b
rows.baseline: No defense: email leakage 5.15%; average utility 58.52%
rows.note: The text reports this SAE-feature ablation result alongside the no-SAE configuration. The outcomes measure privacy and utility, not neuron interpretability or the listed versions.
rows.check: Values are correct per Table 1. The row compares the study's own SAE method with its no-SAE variant on privacy and utility. It is a method-performance comparison, not a measure of any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
